title: The 75% voting participation rule resets its measurement window after a breach to prevent repeat penalties
content:
A.1.6.2.1 requires Aligned Delegates to "maintain a voting participation rate of at least seventy-five percent (75%) over the past six (6) months in all votes they are eligible to cast," with failure a Tier 1 (Procedural) breach, evaluated monthly and measured from the date of formal recognition. Participation counts only for votes where SKY is actually delegated to that delegate.

The subtle part is the anti-recurrence provision. Once a Tier 1 breach has issued, the Core Facilitator "will not issue a further Tier 1 (Procedural) breach solely because the Aligned Delegate's participation rate over the past six (6) months remains below seventy-five percent (75%), provided that the Aligned Delegate has participated in at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the votes for which they were eligible after the most recent breach was issued."

This fixes a genuine defect in rolling-window metrics. A delegate who misses a stretch of votes carries that deficit in the trailing six-month average for months afterward — so a naive rule would issue a fresh breach every monthly evaluation for the same underlying lapse, and under a graduated framework that escalates to derecognition for conduct already sanctioned. Worse, it would leave the delegate with no achievable path back to compliance, which destroys the incentive to resume participating at all.

Resetting the measurement baseline to the breach date makes the metric **forward-looking after enforcement**: the question becomes "have you complied since being told," which is the behaviour the rule actually wants. Historical shortfall is punished once, not continuously.

A.1.6.2.1.2 tightens the same metric from the other end — for Executive Votes, a vote counts only if cast "within three (3) business days of the Executive Vote being posted," so participation cannot be satisfied by voting after the fact. Presence must be timely to count at all.
description: A.1.6.2.1 stops a rolling six-month average from re-triggering Tier 1 breaches month after month: once cited, only votes eligible after the breach count toward the next assessment.
